My phrasebook

Star any question while you practise to keep that item here, whatever row it lives in. It is saved with your farm.

Study calendar

A day is marked when you answer at least one question anywhere in the game; the small number is how many. Dates come from this device's clock and are saved with your farm.

Exam planner

15 minutes a day

A rough guide, not a promise. It replays the game's own review schedule on a copy of your farm, assuming you move the day on once for every real day, that one answer takes about 30 seconds, that already-planted plots are reviewed first and spare time plants new ones, and that about one answer in four is wrong. The date is saved with your farm.

How is my review schedule worked out?

Greetings & Basics Blitz

60 seconds and 3 lives on Normal (see Difficulty). A steady stream of translation questions from your greetings/family/description weeks (rows 1-11) — answer fast, build a combo, and see your score before the clock runs out. The line under each question names the plot a correct answer waters.

Passé Composé Sprint

60 seconds and 3 lives on Normal (see Difficulty). A steady stream of fill-in-the-blank and conjugation questions on the passé composé (rows 21-23) — answer fast, build a combo, and see your score before the clock runs out.

Word Match

Match each French word or phrase with its English card, from your vocabulary and phrase weeks 12-23. Three boards of four pairs. Every right pair waters that plot; a wrong pair costs a life and changes nothing on the farm.

Grammar Gaps

Fill the gap in a grammar example: the verb form, the missing word or the ending. It covers the grammar of weeks 1-11 and 16-23 that Verb Racer and the Sprint do not (the passé composé has its own Sprint). A plot you know well asks you to type the answer.

Listening Pick

Hear a French word, phrase or letter name and pick what it means, from any week. Ten questions; each has its own clock. It uses your browser's own French voice; without one the French is shown on screen instead. A plot you know well asks you to type the meaning.

Word Order Race

Tap the words in the right order to build the French sentence for the English one shown. The sentences are the examples inside the grammar rules of weeks 1-23; a right order waters that grammar plot. Six sentences, each against its own clock; a miss costs only the points.

Verb Racer

Pick the correctly conjugated verb form to advance one step — from your daily-routine/reflexives/comparative weeks (rows 12-15). A steady rival advances on its own every few seconds. First to the finish line wins.

Boutique Dash

A customer wants a colour + garment combination from your shopping-for-clothes weeks (rows 16-18) — pick the matching item from the rack before their patience runs out. 15 customers a shift; correct sales speed the pace up slightly.

Café Rush

A customer orders food or drink from your café weeks (rows 19-23) — pick the matching item before their patience runs out. Every third customer also asks you to confirm the order in the passé composé. 15 customers a shift.

Now confirm the order in the past tense:

The field of words. Every plot is one French fact — water it when it needs water, and watch it slowly stop needing you.

One continuous farm across FREN151 and FREN152, planted in syllabus order. Correct recall grows a plant and stretches the gap before it asks again; a plot that has gone quiet for long enough gets its own sprinkler. Nothing here dies, and nothing here keeps score against you.

This only affects typed answers. On, your spelling of accents has to match exactly (é is not the same as e). Off, accents are ignored when your answer is checked, so é and e count as equal. Multiple-choice questions aren't affected either way.

Water options

Watering and nudging: the first correct answer for a plot each day waters it fully (its interval, ease and growth stage all update). Later correct answers for the same plot that day only nudge its next review a day later. A wrong answer changes nothing, and a plot never loses a stage. The count beside each option is how many plots it can still water right now.

How confident are you? (optional)

i

Purely optional and never blocks answering. Tagging a wrong answer as "Sure" schedules it a little sooner than usual; tagging it "Not sure" is gentler than usual — a confident miss is a bigger gap than an unsure guess. A correct answer isn't affected either way.

i

Typed answers are graded differently by length: a single word (a vocab word, a number, one conjugated form) needs an exact match after minor cleanup, while a full phrase or sentence accepts several valid phrasings — so don't worry about matching a longer answer word-for-word.

i

Reporting doesn't mark your answer correct automatically — it adds it to a queue that gets checked by hand. If it's a genuinely valid phrasing, it gets added so the game accepts it for everyone from then on.

i
